CXXV. a. 155 CXX XVIII. 1372. 24. Mai. 0. A0. — Johann von Dubowa verkauft dem Wanko von Elhenitz seinen Freihof im Dorfe Schestau trm 28 Schock Prager Groschen. Ego Johan de Dubova ad vniuersorum noticiam tam presencium quam futurorum disposui peruenire, quod compos rationis existens propria desuperque snadela amicorum meorum preuia honesto et discreto Wankoni de Elenyc suisque natis et nascendis heredibus curiam meam liberam in villa Ziestow cum agris cultis et incultis pascuis omnibus et singulis prouentibus, in quibuscumque rehus aut substanciis nunc et denno temporis successu instante consistant, ad ipsam speetantibus hereditarie et de spontanea voluntate pro viginti octo sexagenis grossorum Pragensium denanorum integre a dicto Wankone perceptorum presentibus recognosco me rationabiliter vendidisse iuste uendicionis titulo resignando. Et ne buiusmodi uen- dicio in antea in irritum quomodolibet deueniret et inane, cum dis- cretis Jendlino de Chwalin fratre meo karissimo, Smilone de Rowna, Johanne de Bor alias de Rowneho dicto, Raczkone de Hor, curiam suis cum pertinentiis predictam pre impeticione vxoris mee, a qua dictam curiam cum omnibus usufructibus in accessu matrimonialis copule percepi in possessionem, cuiuslibetque hominis et persone iure terre regni Boemie ab olim vsuali er approbata spondeo disbri- gare. Nos quoque Jendlinus de Chwalin, Smilo de Rowneho, Johan nes de Bor, Raczko de Huor, prenominati profitentes pretacte curie alodialis eo, quo prefertur, jure nos fore disbrigatores legittimos vnacum predicto Johanne de Dubowa omnium seriatim premissa hie contenta manu coniuncta et indiuisa solidaque fidei firmitate promit- timus obseruare. Si uero nequiremus ant non curaremus exbrigare memoratam curiam alodialem, quod absit, aliquopiam impetente uel impetentibus extunc preallegato Wankoni aut suis heredibus de tanta hereditatum nostrorum quantitate parte tercia euidenter super- aucta, vbicunque in nostris bonis generaliter congruencius uisum fuerit, ipsi Wunkoni sine quauis uerborum aut operum obuencione se intromittendi damus potestatem plenam. entries.english:
I, Konrad von Trojanow, son of Gregor von Herslag, Ritter, of blessed memory and lawful guardian of the orphans of the late Jeschek von Swietlik, make known that, after careful deliberation and on the mature advice of my friends, for the orphans' benefit and common good and to avert any loss they might suffer from payment of a dowry, I have lawfully sold to the venerable and religious Heinrich, Abt zu Hohenfurt, and the whole convent the farm commonly called Ostrow, with its good and valuable ploughland, and the village in which it lies, as well as the neighboring village commonly called Klesczin. Their hereditary boundaries and markers include two mills and a certain perpetual rent in those villages of six schocks and twenty-five Prague groschen and five Viennese pfennigs, together with pastures, meadows, brush, woods, streams, fisheries, and all other rights belonging to the farm and villages. I have sold these holdings for 127 schocks of Prague groschen and 60 Viennese pfennigs, to be held as the orphans held them by paternal inheritance. The abbot and convent have paid the sum in full; from it I have paid in full the dowry assigned to the orphans' mother, which her second husband, their stepfather Sobyessyn, had firmly demanded after her death. In good faith, together with my brothers Beness von Herslag and Nikolaus von Perny, I jointly promise as lawful guarantors and defenders under Bohemian land law to defend and clear these goods against the orphans and any other person. If the orphans, when they come of age, should themselves challenge the abbot or convent over the property, or be induced to do so, we promise to protect the monastery from that challenge for three full years and three days. If we fail, each of us must immediately enter customary surety in the town of Rosenberg, with two horses and one servant, in a house appointed by the abbot or convent, and remain there until the monastery has been compensated for all claimed losses and the full purchase price has been repaid. This charter is sealed by the three guarantors, Konrad, Beness, and Nikolaus. Peter von Rosenberg, Trojan von Brzyezie, and Marquard von Poreschin also append their seals as witnesses. Given on the feast of Saint Prisca in 1372. The six small seals hang from parchment strips; all are in white wax except seal d, which is red. Seal a bears a shield with a rooster’s head and neck, with the legend “Seal of Konrad von Troyan.” Seal b bears a shield with a cup, with the legend “Seal of Beness von Herslag.” Seal c is a helmet whose crest is a man’s upper body, with the legend “Seal of Nikolaus von Perny.” Seal d is Peter von Rosenberg’s small seal, described in no. CIV. Seal e bears a helmet with a wing as its crest, with the legend “Seal of Trojan of Dubrawicz.” Seal f is the previously described seal of Marquard von Poreschin, no. CXXV a.

I, Johann of Dubowa, make known to all present and future people that, being of sound mind and having first taken the advice of my friends, I have, of my own free will, lawfully sold as a freehold to the honorable and prudent Wanko of Elhenitz and his children and future heirs my free farm in the village of Ziestow, with its cultivated and uncultivated fields, pastures, and every revenue and appurtenance, whatever its form or substance now or at any time to come. I acknowledge that I have received the full price of twenty-eight sexagenae of Prague groschen from the aforesaid Wanko. To prevent this sale from ever being invalidated, since I received this farm with all its usufruct into my possession from my wife at the time of our marriage, I promise to defend it against any claim by her or by any other person according to the law of the Kingdom of Bohemia long established and approved. Together with me, my beloved brother Jendlin of Chwalin, Smilo of Rowna, Johann of Bor, also called of Rowneho, and Raczko of Hor, jointly and without division, promise in firm good faith to act as lawful defenders of the aforesaid freehold and observe all the foregoing terms. If we cannot or do not clear the freehold from any claim, which may God forbid, then the aforesaid Wanko or his heirs may take possession, without any objection in word or deed, of an amount from our hereditary properties that is demonstrably one third greater in value, wherever among our properties seems most suitable. Otherwise, if we do not surrender that increased one-third share in the manner stated, two of us, when summoned, shall be bound to enter customary surety, without deceit or fraud, in a suitable lodging in the city of Krumau at Wanko’s request, and not leave until we have surrendered to him the increased third together with the original property and paid all damages arising from it that have been lawfully proved. To confirm and secure all the foregoing, we have attached our seals together with the seal of the aforesaid Johann of Dubowa. Given on 24 May 1372, the Monday after the feast of the Holy Trinity. Five small seals hang from parchment strips in white wax. Seals a and b show the upper body of a man swinging a sword; the legend on a is unreadable because of the poor impression, while b reads “Seal of Jaskon of Chwalin.” Seal c shows a bull’s head, with the legend “Seal of Smil of Rowna.” Seal d bears a shield with the image of a goat, with the legend “Seal of Johann of Bor.” Seal e bears the Harach arms, with a helmet above the shield whose crest is a stag’s antlers, and the legend “Seal of Raczko of Hor.”
